learning_outcomes.text: Student possesses organized knowledge regarding transient states in electrical circuits, three-phase circuits, two-port networks, transmission systems, and nonlinear circuits.

Student knows mathematical methods necessary for describing and analyzing the operation of electrical circuits in transient states, three-phase circuits, two-port networks, transmission systems, and nonlinear circuits.
Student is able to use learned methods to analyze electrical systems.
Student is able to calculate and measure transient waveforms in electrical circuits.
Student is able to calculate and measure currents, voltages, and powers in symmetrical and asymmetrical three-phase systems.
Student is able to write and solve state equations of a linear electrical circuit.
Student understands the need for continuous self-education and raising professional competencies.
Student is aware of the responsibility to act professionally and adhere to professional ethics principles.

syllabus_topics: Auditorium classes are conducted according to the lecture topics.

Transient states in electrical circuits: Classical method of analysis for transient states in first and second-order circuits. Laplace transform and its properties, Dirac delta. Application of Laplace transform to the analysis of transient states in linear electrical circuits (operational method). Circuit elements in the operational domain. Operational impedance and admittance. State equation method. Three-phase circuits: Three-wire and four-wire three-phase systems, symmetrical and asymmetrical. Calculation of voltages and currents in three-phase circuits, vector diagrams. Power in three-phase circuits, measurement of power in three-phase circuits. Determining phase sequence. Method of symmetrical components. Fault conditions in three-phase circuits. Two-port networks: Terminal description of two-port networks. Impedances and transfer functions of two-port networks. Symmetries of two-port networks. Interconnection of two-port networks. Wave description of two-port networks. Transmission systems: Transfer function of a transmission system. Impulse and step response of a transmission system. Stability of transmission systems. Frequency characteristics of transmission systems. Nonlinear electrical circuits.

Example exercise topics: superposition principle, Thevenin's theorem, voltage source characteristics, sinusoidal current circuits – equivalent models, series RLC connection, magnetic couplings, examination of two-port networks, three-phase systems, transient states in first and second-order circuits, electrical circuits with nonlinear elements.
teaching_methods: Practice method (doing tasks at the blackboard)
assessment_rules: A positive grade from auditorium classes, laboratory classes, and the exam is required to pass the lectures. For auditorium classes, attendance and a positive evaluation based on tests and activity during classes are required. For laboratory classes, attendance and a positive evaluation based on the completion of laboratory exercises and activity during classes are required. Passing the module is possible after passing all laboratory classes.
